rationale: The screen is a product listing page titled 'Shop medicines'. It features a main content area displaying various product cards in a grid format. The left sidebar contains navigation links with small text. Above the products, there are dropdowns for filtering ('All Pain Relief Vitamins Personal Care First Aid') and sorting. The product information (name, description, price) is present but the text size appears small across the board.. To continue auditing the user journey, I need to test the filtering functionality to see how the interface handles selection changes. Clicking the current filter dropdown (@e11) is the most logical next step to explore the product discovery path beyond just scrolling. [Friction observed: The font size in the left navigation menu and the small text labels on the product cards create significant visual strain and difficulty for low-vision users. The dropdown menus (@e11, @e12) are functional but require precise interaction.]
